chunk_findings.detail: `FakeLane.steer` checks only whether the handle has the `steer` capability and then records the text, so it succeeds even after the fake lane has been stopped or its script is complete. For example, construct `FakeLane(capabilities=("steer",))`, start a handle, call `stop(handle)` (whose `status` then reports `state="stopped"`), and then call `steer(handle, "next")`; the method returns `L.ok("recorded")` and appends `"next"` to `handle.steered`. A real lane cannot be steered after it has exited or been stopped, so tests driving swarm/ETA behaviour through this fake can falsely conclude that post-stop steering worked. The method should also reject steering when `h.stopped` is true or `h.cursor >= len(h.script)`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/lanes.py:FakeLane.steer

chunk_findings.detail: The manifest shows this change adds the new Lane port in `ddflow/adapters/lanes.py` and `ddflow/adapters/fakes/lanes.py`, but it also modifies `ddflow/services/lane_driver.py` to re-export the contract/registry. [r-adapters] says a new port touches only its own files and that external dependencies go through a port in `ddflow/adapters`; a service module outside `ddflow/adapters` is not one of the port’s own files. This creates a second public import path for the Lane port in a shared service file, so later changes to that shim can collide with the port implementation and violate the “one place” intent of the rule.

chunk_findings.detail: The new documentation states that the Lane port is `ddflow/adapters/lanes.py` while its default adapter is `ddflow/services/lane_headless.py`. The change’s conformance requires the port Protocol to live in `ddflow/adapters` next to its default adapter and registry, and [r-adapters] requires the external dependency (launching and watching an agent process) to be behind a port in `ddflow/adapters`. As documented, the default implementation of the port is outside the adapters package, so changing or swapping the default adapter touches both the port/registry and a service module rather than one place; if the service module is not imported, `driver_for("process-headless")` can return `unavailable` despite the docs calling it the default adapter. This violates [r-adapters].

chunk_findings.detail: The `settle` helper uses wall-clock `time.time()` for its 10-second deadline. If the system clock is stepped forward by more than 10 seconds while the real `ProcessHeadless` conformance test is waiting (e.g. NTP correction, VM/host clock adjustment, or another test that manipulates `time.time`), the loop exits even though `lane.status(h).state` may still be `"running"`; the next assertion then fails with `running` instead of `exited`. A monotonic clock (`time.monotonic()`) or the lane's own timeout would avoid this environment-dependent failure.

chunk_findings.detail: `FakeLane.status` extracts `session` from the entire scripted `h.script`, ignoring `h.cursor`. For example, construct `FakeLane(transcript=[("text", {}), ("started", {"session": "abc"})])` and start it with a normal `LaunchSpec` whose `event_buffer` is large enough not to drop events. Immediately after `start`, `h.cursor == 0`, so `events()` has not replayed anything and `status()` correctly reports `state="running"` and `exit_code=None`; nevertheless `status().session` is `"abc"` because the `started` event is in the script but has not been observed/replayed. This makes the fake report a session before the lane has actually emitted the started event, which is inconsistent with the same function’s “script read” gating and can fail conformance against an adapter that only exposes the session after the started event is observed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/lanes.py:106

chunk_findings.detail: The documentation states that the default adapter implementation is `process-headless` in `ddflow/services/lane_headless.py`, while the required conformance is that the port’s Protocol and its default adapter live together in `ddflow/adapters`. With this layout, a caller or test that wants the default Lane adapter must import `ddflow.services.lane_headless` rather than the adapter package, so the port cannot be exercised or swapped without pulling in the services layer; that breaks the adapters boundary required by [D-adapters-answers] and [r-adapters].

chunk_findings.detail: The conformance helper `lane_conformance` is meant to prove the `Lane` contract, but it never exercises `cleanup` even though the stated contract includes cleanup. It only calls `start`, `events`, `status`, `steer`, `stop`, and a refused start. Therefore an adapter or fake whose `cleanup` raises, leaks a child process/temporary directory, or returns a failed `Result` can still pass `test_the_adapter_passes_the_conformance_cases` and the generic fake conformance case, because no assertion ever calls `lane.cleanup(h)` or checks its idempotence/result.

chunk_findings.detail: The requirement says “unavailable is never passed”, but `steer` returns `L.unavailable("the fake lane was built without the steer capability")` when the handle lacks the `"steer"` capability. A default `FakeLane()` built without `"steer"` passed to `steer` yields an `unavailable` result to the caller, violating the stated CONFORMANCE property. It should fail or record the steer instead of passing `unavailable`.

This violates [r-adapters] and the stated conformance that the port’s default adapter lives next to the port in `ddflow/adapters`. The default adapter must be next to/registrable from the port itself.

chunk_findings.detail: `advertise` now accepts `Capable`, but the `Lane` protocol no longer declares `capabilities` and does not inherit from `Capable`. As a result, a typed caller that obtains a `Lane` (e.g. from `driver_for`) and invokes `L.advertise(driver, wanted)` will fail static type checking: the type checker sees `Lane` as incompatible with `Capable`, even though the runtime object has the attribute. The public contract’s docstring still says a lane object carries capabilities, so the type says the opposite. This is not exercised by the runtime tests because the actual objects do carry `capabilities`.

chunk_findings.detail: The Lane port still does not keep its default adapter in the adapters package. `BUILTIN_TRANSPORTS` maps `process-headless` to `ddflow.services.lane_headless`, and `driver_for` lazily imports that service module (line 170). Thus `from ddflow.adapters.lanes import driver_for; driver_for("process-headless")` pulls the services layer into the port, and a conformance test cannot exercise or swap the default Lane adapter without importing `ddflow.services.lane_headless`. This is the same placement violation as previous finding 5; the current code does not move the adapter into `ddflow/adapters`, and the docstring at line 132 still says the default lives in services. It violates [r-adapters] and the stated conformance that the port Protocol and default adapter live together in `ddflow/adapters`.

This violates [r-adapters] and the stated conformance that the default adapter lives next to the port. Concrete failure: after importing only `ddflow.adapters.lanes`, `driver_for("process-headless")` returns `unavailable` because the registration side effect in `ddflow/services/lane_headless.py` has not run, even though the docs present `process-headless` as the default adapter; callers must reach into the services layer to use or swap the default implementation.

chunk_findings.detail: The conformance helper is supposed to prove the `Lane` contract, and the stated contract includes `cleanup`, but the helper never calls `cleanup` (nor asserts that it exists, is safe after `stop`, or is idempotent). It only exercises `start`, `events`, `status`, `steer`, `stop`, `advertise`, and a refused start, and the generic `CONFORMANCE` entry at line 88 plus `test_the_adapter_passes_the_conformance_cases` at line 100 use this same helper. Therefore an adapter or fake whose `cleanup` raises, leaks a child process/temporary directory, or returns a failed `Result` can still pass these new conformance tests; for example, a `FakeLane.cleanup` that raises `RuntimeError("leak")` would not be observed because `cleanup` is never invoked. This is the same gap reported previously and it still holds in the current conformance helper.

The change's CONFORMANCE list explicitly requires "unavailable is never passed." A default `FakeLane()` has capabilities `("interrupt", "usage", "tool_events")` — no `"steer"` — so `lane.start(spec)` followed by `lane.steer(handle, "please stop")` returns an `unavailable` result to the caller, passing the forbidden value. The previous report of this defect still holds because the current code path is unchanged.

This is the same unresolved defect as previous findings #2/#5 and violates [r-adapters] plus the CONFORMANCE requirement that the port’s Protocol and default adapter live together in `ddflow/adapters`. The new auto-import does not answer the layout requirement; it only means a caller does not explicitly import the services module before calling `driver_for`, while the new port still reaches into `ddflow.services` instead of touching only its own adapter files.

An adapter or fake that returns `unavailable` here should fail conformance, not pass; as written, `lane_conformance` would pass the broken `FakeLane.steer` from previous finding 4 and would fail a correct implementation that records the steer or raises instead. Therefore, an adapter or fake whose `cleanup` method is broken, leaks resources, or returns a failed result will still pass `test_the_adapter_passes_the_conformance_cases` and the generic fake conformance case without any test exercising or asserting its behavior.

chunk_findings.detail: `FakeLane.stop` marks the handle as ended by setting `h.cursor = len(h.script)`, while `FakeLane.status` reports `events=h.cursor`. Given a fake with a non-empty transcript, start a handle, call `stop` before consuming any events, then call `status`: it returns `state="stopped"` and `events=len(transcript)` (and may also report a `session` from a `started` event that was never emitted), even though `list(lane.events(handle))` yields no events. A real lane stopped before emitting those events should not report them as already emitted, so the fake can pass conformance or swarm/ETA cases that would fail against the real adapter.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/lanes.py:FakeLane.stop

chunk_findings.detail: The `Lane` protocol still does not declare or inherit `capabilities`, but `advertise` accepts `Capable | Lane` and immediately dereferences `driver.capabilities`. A typed caller that uses the port’s own return type—`driver_for(...) -> Lane | Result`, narrows away `Result`, and calls `lanes.advertise(driver, {"steer"})`—has an invalid annotation because the narrowed `driver` is a `Lane`, and the `Lane` protocol has no `capabilities` member. The runtime conformance test does not answer this: it only proves the shipped adapter/fake happen to carry the attribute; it does not make `Lane` satisfy `Capable` or prevent a lane object that passes `isinstance(..., Lane)` but lacks capabilities from crashing in `advertise`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/lanes.py:advertise

chunk_findings.detail: `stop` marks an early stop by doing `h.cursor = len(h.script)`, and `status()` later returns `events=h.cursor`. That makes a stopped lane report as many events as a full replay even when `events()` was never called. For example, start `FakeLane([("out", {}), ("exit", {})])` with a large `event_buffer`, call `stop(h)` before `events(h)`, then `status(h)`; the fake returns `state="stopped"` and `events=2` while no lane event was ever yielded. A real stopped lane would report only the events it actually produced, so the fake over-reports progress and can make ETA/conformance tests pass when the lane was cut short. `stop` should not advance the replay cursor; `status` should derive `stopped` from `h.stopped` without treating unread script entries as read.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/lanes.py:95 FakeLane.stop / FakeLane.status

chunk_findings.detail: The previous finding still holds. `Lane` remains a `Protocol` without a `capabilities` member and does not inherit `Capable`, yet `advertise` is typed as `def advertise(driver: Capable | Lane, ...)` and then accesses `driver.capabilities`. A typed caller that gets a `Lane` from `driver_for` and calls `advertise(lane, {"steer"})` fails static type checking because `Lane` has no `capabilities` attribute. The cited probe `test_the_adapter_and_the_fake_satisfy_the_port` only checks the runtime objects structurally; it cannot catch and does not fix the static-contract mismatch.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/lanes.py:advertise

chunk_findings.detail: The cited probe for the confirmed previous defect does not answer it. `isinstance(lh.ProcessHeadless(), L.Lane)` and `isinstance(FakeLane(), L.Lane)` are runtime checks; for a runtime-checkable `typing.Protocol`, `isinstance` verifies only the members declared on `L.Lane`, so it cannot detect that `L.Lane` does not declare `capabilities` or is not assignable to `Capable`. A typed caller that obtains a `Lane` and calls `L.advertise(lane, wanted)` would still fail static type checking under mypy/pyright, exactly the confirmed issue.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_adapter_lanes.py:test_the_adapter_and_the_fake_satisfy_the_port

Thus `from ddflow.adapters.lanes import driver_for; driver_for("process-headless")` pulls the services layer into the port, and a conformance test cannot exercise or swap the default Lane adapter without importing `ddflow.services.lane_headless`. This is the same placement violation as previous finding 5; the current code does not move the adapter into `ddflow/adapters`, and the docstring at line 132 still says the default lives in services. It violates [r-adapters] and the stated conformance that the port Protocol and default adapter live together in `ddflow/adapters`.

chunk_findings.detail: The new port documentation still places the default Lane adapter in `ddflow/services/lane_headless.py` and says it registers itself only as a side effect of that service module, while the port/registry are documented as `ddflow/adapters/lanes.py`. This violates [r-adapters] and the stated conformance that the default adapter lives next to the port. Concrete failure: after importing only `ddflow.adapters.lanes`, `driver_for("process-headless")` returns `unavailable` because the registration side effect in `ddflow/services/lane_headless.py` has not run, even though the docs present `process-headless` as the default adapter; callers must reach into the services layer to use or swap the default implementation.

chunk_findings.detail: The conformance helper is supposed to prove the `Lane` contract, and the stated contract includes `cleanup`, but the helper never calls `cleanup` (nor asserts that it exists, is safe after `stop`, or is idempotent). It only exercises `start`, `events`, `status`, `steer`, `stop`, `advertise`, and a refused start, and the generic `CONFORMANCE` entry at line 88 plus `test_the_adapter_passes_the_conformance_cases` at line 100 use this same helper. Therefore an adapter or fake whose `cleanup` raises, leaks a child process/temporary directory, or returns a failed `Result` can still pass these new conformance tests; for example, a `FakeLane.cleanup` that raises `RuntimeError("leak")` would not be observed because `cleanup` is never invoked. This is the same gap reported previously and it still holds in the current conformance helper.

chunk_findings.detail: `FakeLane.steer` still returns `L.unavailable("the fake lane was built without the steer capability")` when the handle lacks `"steer"`. A default `FakeLane()` has capabilities `("interrupt", "usage", "tool_events")` — no `"steer"` — so `lane.start(spec)` followed by `lane.steer(handle, "please stop")` returns an `unavailable` result to the caller, passing the forbidden value. chunk_findings.detail: `FakeLane.stop` marks the handle as ended by setting `h.cursor = len(h.script)`, while `FakeLane.status` reports `events=h.cursor`. Given a fake with a non-empty transcript, start a handle, call `stop` before consuming any events, then call `status`: it returns `state="stopped"` and `events=len(transcript)` (and may also report a `session` from a `started` event that was never emitted), even though `list(lane.events(handle))` yields no events. A real lane stopped before emitting those events should not report them as already emitted, so the fake can pass conformance or swarm/ETA cases that would fail against the real adapter.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/lanes.py:FakeLane.stop

chunk_findings.detail: The `Lane` protocol still does not declare or inherit `capabilities`, but `advertise` accepts `Capable | Lane` and immediately dereferences `driver.capabilities`. A typed caller that uses the port’s own return type—`driver_for(...) -> Lane | Result`, narrows away `Result`, and calls `lanes.advertise(driver, {"steer"})`—has an invalid annotation because the narrowed `driver` is a `Lane`, and the `Lane` protocol has no `capabilities` member. The runtime conformance test does not answer this: it only proves the shipped adapter/fake happen to carry the attribute; it does not make `Lane` satisfy `Capable` or prevent a lane object that passes `isinstance(..., Lane)` but lacks capabilities from crashing in `advertise`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/lanes.py:advertise

chunk_findings.detail: `stop` marks an early stop by doing `h.cursor = len(h.script)`, and `status()` later returns `events=h.cursor`. That makes a stopped lane report as many events as a full replay even when `events()` was never called. For example, start `FakeLane([("out", {}), ("exit", {})])` with a large `event_buffer`, call `stop(h)` before `events(h)`, then `status(h)`; the fake returns `state="stopped"` and `events=2` while no lane event was ever yielded. A real stopped lane would report only the events it actually produced, so the fake over-reports progress and can make ETA/conformance tests pass when the lane was cut short. `stop` should not advance the replay cursor; `status` should derive `stopped` from `h.stopped` without treating unread script entries as read.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/lanes.py:95 FakeLane.stop / FakeLane.status

chunk_findings.detail: The previous finding still holds. `Lane` remains a `Protocol` without a `capabilities` member and does not inherit `Capable`, yet `advertise` is typed as `def advertise(driver: Capable | Lane, ...)` and then accesses `driver.capabilities`. A typed caller that gets a `Lane` from `driver_for` and calls `advertise(lane, {"steer"})` fails static type checking because `Lane` has no `capabilities` attribute. The cited probe `test_the_adapter_and_the_fake_satisfy_the_port` only checks the runtime objects structurally; it cannot catch and does not fix the static-contract mismatch.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/lanes.py:advertise

chunk_findings.detail: The cited probe for the confirmed previous defect does not answer it. `isinstance(lh.ProcessHeadless(), L.Lane)` and `isinstance(FakeLane(), L.Lane)` are runtime checks; for a runtime-checkable `typing.Protocol`, `isinstance` verifies only the members declared on `L.Lane`, so it cannot detect that `L.Lane` does not declare `capabilities` or is not assignable to `Capable`. A typed caller that obtains a `Lane` and calls `L.advertise(lane, wanted)` would still fail static type checking under mypy/pyright, exactly the confirmed issue.
